study_identification_part.si4_title: Contrasting Case-Control and Normative Reference Approaches to Capture Clinically Relevant Structural Brain Abnormalities in Patients With First-Episode Psychosis Who Are Antipsychotic Naive

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate whether baseline deviations from a normative reference in subcortical volumes better predict antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes in antipsychotic-naive first-episode psychosis (FEP).

nm1_model_origin.detail: BrainCharts reference models trained on 58,836 healthy individuals across the lifespan (Rutherford et al., 2022), applied via PCNtoolkit/BrainCharts and calibrated to UAB controls following Dinga et al. (2021).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Negative deviations in caudate, putamen, and ventral diencephalon predicted better antipsychotic response, outperforming raw subcortical volumes.
